narrative.overview: QuizIt redesigns around a single refusal: this is not a dashboard with quiz features bolted onto cards. It is staged as a match. Every surface reads as a character-select or versus screen from 90s arcade fighting games: two opposing corners, a HUD strip of hard numbers, a select-grid of modes, and a clock that means something. Two combat colors carry the surface at Committed strength: P1 electric cyan for the player's own corner and primary actions, P2 hot coral for the opponent's corner, destructive states, and urgency. They never blend into a gradient.
keyCharacteristics: Two-corner color opposition (P1 cyan vs. P2 coral), never mixed
Hard-edged cabinet panels — small radius, high-contrast borders, no blur/glass
Condensed arcade-marquee display type; tabular monospace for every number
State changes never rely on color alone
Numeric deltas render inline, always visible

rules.name: The Two-Corner Rule
rules.body: Primary and secondary never appear together as a gradient or blend. If a screen needs both, they sit in physically opposed positions.

rules.name: The Timer Rule
rules.body: Amber is reserved for timer/urgency countdowns only. It never brands a resting element.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow/kicker label above a heading, anywhere. The heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Rest-State Rule
rules.body: No element glows or elevates at rest. Glow is earned by hover, focus, or selection.

dos: Do pair every state change with a label, icon, or motion — never color alone.
Do show numeric deltas inline next to the value they changed, always visible.
Do keep P1 (cyan) and P2 (coral) physically separated.
Do set every score, timer, rating, and rank in the numeric/monospace face with tabular figures.
donts: Don't use an eyebrow/kicker label above a page heading.
Don't use gradient text or a gradient fill on any word or number.
Don't default to rounded-xl/rounded-2xl panel corners.
Don't ship a same-size icon+heading+text card grid as page structure when the content has real hierarchy.
